permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.subtitle: Fine-tune when the agent can run tools without asking. Built-in smart policy handles most cases — use this page for exceptions.
permissions.overviewIntro: When the agent edits files, runs shell commands, or calls other tools, Prism decides whether to run automatically, show a confirmation card, or block the action.
permissions.overviewBulletDefault: By default, smart policy applies: in-project edits and common dev commands (git, package managers) run without a prompt; deletes always ask; operations outside the project are restricted.
permissions.overviewBulletAllow: Allow rules and allowed paths add exceptions — matching calls skip the confirmation card.
permissions.overviewBulletDeny: Deny rules block matching operations even when smart policy would allow them. Some safety limits (e.g. deleting outside the project) cannot be overridden.
permissions.overviewBulletPrompt: When nothing matches, you see the permission card in chat — Allow, Deny, or Always (Always adds an allow rule here).
permissions.rulesSectionDesc: Optional exceptions on top of built-in smart policy. Open a row to edit in the side panel.
permissions.allowedPathsListDesc: Extra trusted directories outside the project root — not needed for paths inside the open project.
permissions.allowRulesListDesc: Tool calls that match skip the confirmation card. Composer "Always" choices appear here.
permissions.denyRulesListDesc: Matching operations are blocked even when smart policy would allow them.
permissions.noProjectHint: Open a project to test path-based rules against a project root.
permissions.readonlyDesc: Block file edits and shell commands. Reads and search still work.
permissions.projectRootHint: Current project root (always trusted for in-project edits): {{path}}
permissions.allowRulesPlaceholder:
# Examples
Bash(git *)
Bash(pnpm install*)
Edit(**/drafts/*)
WebFetch(arxiv.org/*)

toolsCatalog.sectionDesc: Allow/Deny rules only matter for gated tools — file edits, shell, and network fetches that can trigger a confirmation card.
toolsCatalog.alwaysAllowedNote: Always allowed (no rules needed): read, grep, glob, question, task, skill, todowrite.

permissions.docsSummary: Syntax, priority, slash commands, and Expert presets
permissions.docsBuiltin: You do not need rules for everyday work inside the project. Smart policy already allows in-project edits, git, package managers, and experiment runs; prompts on delete; and blocks dangerous operations outside the project. This page is for exceptions only.
permissions.docsPriority: Read-only mode → built-in safety deny → your deny rules → Plan agent overrides → your allow rules → allowed paths → built-in smart policy → confirmation card.
permissions.docsSyntax: Format: ToolName(pattern). Use * for one path segment, ** for recursive paths. For Bash, the pattern matches the full command string.
permissions.syntaxExampleEdit: Edit(**/drafts/*) — edits under any drafts folder
permissions.syntaxExampleDelete: Delete(*.log) — delete log files (still subject to safety limits)
permissions.syntaxExampleDenyBash: Bash(curl *|*bash*) — block curl or piped bash
permissions.docsCommands: Action commands (/compile, /setup) run locally and bypass this gate. AI commands send instructions to the agent — subsequent tool calls follow these rules. Template !`cmd` snippets run during command expand and must pass Bash rules here.
permissions.docsExperts: Expert permission presets (Standard / Full / Read-only) are configured per expert profile and are separate from these global rules.
permissions.testerDesc: Preview how saved rules would treat a tool call.
permissions.testerToolHint: OpenCode tool name — see the list in Allow/Deny rule editors.
permissions.testerTargetHint: Full bash command, or file path for Edit / Delete / Move.
permissions.testerIdleHint: Enter a tool and path or command, then run preview.

editor.syntaxHint: Format: ToolName(pattern). Use * for one path segment, ** for recursive paths. Lines starting with # are comments.

allowed-paths.intro: One absolute path per line — for directories outside the project root only.
allowed-paths.helpBody: The open project root is already trusted: in-project edits do not need to be listed here. Use allowed paths when the agent must touch files elsewhere — shared data folders, external build output, a second library on disk, etc. Each line must be an absolute path. File tools (Edit, Delete, Move) treat paths under these directories like in-project paths. Shell (bash) is not controlled by this list — use Allow/Deny rules for commands instead.
allowed-paths.helpNote: Tip: use a trailing slash for directories (e.g. /Users/me/shared-data/). Listing a folder inside the project is redundant.

allow-rules.intro: One rule per line. Matching tool calls run without a confirmation card.
allow-rules.helpBody: Use allow rules for commands or file patterns you want to auto-approve. Composer "Always" adds entries here. Allow rules cannot override built-in safety denies (e.g. deleting outside the project).

deny-rules.intro: One rule per line. Matching operations are blocked immediately.
deny-rules.helpBody: Deny rules take priority over allow rules and smart policy defaults. Use them to block specific commands, domains, or file patterns.
